title: A bead in more viscous fluid
hook: Change fluid viscosity and predict terminal speed.
misconception: terminal speed doubles when fluid viscosity doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v_t = 2Δρgr²/(9η) to compare terminal speed when fluid viscosity changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a small sphere denser than the fluid in Stokes flow with fixed radius gravity and density difference, v_t = 2Δρgr²/(9η). When fluid viscosity doubles, terminal speed becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v_t = 2Δρgr²/(9η); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a small sphere denser than the fluid in Stokes flow with fixed radius gravity and density difference, with a nonzero initial result. If fluid viscosity triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on terminal speed?
recall.why: Apply v_t = 2Δρgr²/(9η) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
